title: Microsoft Dataverse: management MCP server for building and governing MCP servers
summary: Hold: the preview reference does not say the management server is free, and the published DLP PowerShell example is not a runnable call. The cited administration paths are supported, but the connector-policy row needs a clearer consumption boundary and the action rating understates the approaching automatic rollout.

claims.where: front matter: licensing.model; Cost and licensing; rationale: cost
claims.claim: A licensing model specific to the management server has not been published.
claims.quote: Searched: '"MCPManagement" licensing pricing management server'; '"management MCP server" "licensing"'. Opened management reference, Copilot Studio billing-licensing and Agent 365 tooling-servers-overview; none specifies a management-server licence.

claims.claim: The management preview reference does not publish a charge.
claims.quote: Searched: '"MCPManagement" licensing pricing management server'; '"management MCP server" quota rate limits licensing'. Opened the complete mcp-management reference and billing-licensing; the reference contains no charge or pricing statement.

claims.claim: The preview reference states that there is no charge.
claims.quote: Searched: '"MCPManagement" licensing pricing management server'; '"management MCP server" "licensing"'. Opened mcp-management in full and billing-licensing. Neither states that the management server is free.
claims.fix: Replace the first sentence with 'Licensing for the management server is not yet published, and the preview reference does not publish a charge.' Silence about pricing is not a no-charge commitment.

claims.claim: Consuming Copilot Studio agents may use Copilot Credits under their existing billing model.
claims.quote: By using the pay-as-you-go meter, at the end of each month, your organization pays only for the actual number of Copilot Credits its agents use during the month.

claims.claim: Premium connector licensing depends on the consuming product and licence rather than being established by the management reference.
claims.quote: The standalone Copilot Studio subscription lets you build agents on any supported channel and connect to any data using premium connectors.

claims.claim: Dataverse service protection API limits constrain underlying Dataverse API calls.
claims.quote: To ensure consistent availability and performance for everyone, Dataverse applies limits to how APIs are used. These limits detect when client applications make extraordinary demands on server resources.

claims.claim: The cited service protection limits are not a published management-server quota or pricing meter.
claims.quote: Searched: '"management MCP server" quota rate limits licensing'. Opened mcp-management, api-limits and billing-licensing; none describes Dataverse service protection limits as a management-server quota or pricing meter.

claims.claim: The Dataverse data-endpoint availability switch is under Manage > Environments > environment > Settings > Product > Features > Dataverse Model Context Protocol > Allow MCP clients to interact with Dataverse MCP server.
claims.quote:
Select Manage > Environments.
Select the Environment Name ... select Settings. ... select Product > Features. ... locate Dataverse Model Context Protocol ... Allow MCP clients to interact with Dataverse MCP server

claims.claim: An automation equivalent for the environment-wide Dataverse MCP availability switch is not documented.
claims.quote: Searched: Dataverse MCP organization Web API enable disable; '"Allow MCP clients" "Power Platform API" PowerShell pac'; Dataverse MCP PowerShell disable. Opened MCP configuration and CLI reference; results document client allow-list automation, not the global switch.

claims.claim: Microsoft has not established that the Dataverse data-endpoint switches grant, revoke or govern access to the management endpoint.
claims.quote: Searched: '"management MCP" disable admin DLP access control audit permissions'; '"MCPManagement" admin UI disable Power Platform API pac admin settings'. Opened mcp-management and Dataverse MCP configuration; neither establishes this relationship.

claims.claim: Dataverse MCP client permissions are edited under the environment's Features > Dataverse Model Context Protocol > Advanced Settings > client > Is Enabled.
claims.quote:
Select Advanced Settings.
The list of available clients is shown. Open the client record you want.
On the MCP client record, set Is Enabled to Yes.

claims.claim: dataverse mcp allow <appId> allows the application as a Dataverse MCP client in the current profile's environment.
claims.quote:
Ensure that a Microsoft Entra application is in the Dataverse MCP allowed clients list for the current profile's environment.

dataverse mcp allow <appId> [options]

claims.claim: The Dataverse CLI reference describes a preview feature.
claims.quote:
Dataverse CLI reference (preview)

This is a preview feature.

claims.claim: The mcp allow command requires Dataverse admin permissions on the target environment.
claims.quote: The authenticated user must have Dataverse admin permissions on the target environment.

claims.claim: Dataverse MCP client allow listing applies only to the /api/mcp agent entrypoint.
claims.quote: MCP allow listing applies only to the /api/mcp agent entrypoint. MCP-named custom APIs are regular Dataverse APIs and aren't restricted by this setting.

claims.claim: Registered MCP servers are blocked in Microsoft 365 admin center at Agents > Tools > Registry > MCP server > Block.
claims.quote:
Select Agents > Tools, and then select the Registry tab.
Select an MCP server from the list to open its overview pane.
Select Block to restrict the server across your organization

claims.claim: Blocking a registered MCP server disables all the tools it exposes.
claims.quote: Blocking an MCP server disables all the tools it exposes. This action targets the server component, rather than a whole plugin package.

claims.claim: Individual tool toggles are on the selected MCP server's Tools tab.
claims.quote:
Select the Tools tab. The list shows every tool the server exposes, along with its description and an Enabled or Disabled toggle.
Turn individual tools on or off as needed.

claims.claim: Individual tool control is limited to supported registered server types and gateway-mediated experiences.
claims.quote:
Tool-level granular control is rolling out to tenants and supports only specific types of MCP servers registered on Agent 365.
The Agent 365 Tooling Gateway enforces the policy at runtime for supported tools and experiences that use the gateway.

claims.claim: The cited Agent 365 controls are not documented to govern direct calls to the management endpoint.
claims.quote: Searched: '"MCPManagement" "access" "control"'; Agent 365 block MCP server tools Microsoft Graph API registry. Opened management reference, Agent 365 management and tooling overview; none establishes direct-management-endpoint enforcement.

claims.claim: An API equivalent for the registered-server Block control is not documented in the checked references.
claims.quote: Searched: Agent 365 block MCP server tools Microsoft Graph API registry; '"MCP server" "Graph API" "block" "Tools" registry beta'. Opened Agent 365 MCP management; results describe UI blocking, not a corresponding Microsoft Graph operation.

claims.claim: Classic data-policy creation is reached at Power Platform admin center > Security > Data and privacy > Data policy > New Policy.
claims.quote:
select Security ... select Data and privacy.
On the Data protection and privacy page, select Data policy.
Select an existing policy ... or select New Policy to create a new policy to configure.

claims.claim: New-DlpPolicy (Microsoft.PowerApps.Administration.PowerShell) is a runnable DLP policy-creation call.
claims.quote:
New-DlpPolicy -NewPolicy <Object> [-ApiVersion <String>] [<CommonParameters>]

New-DlpPolicy -NewPolicy $NewPolicy

Creates a new policy with the $NewPolicy object.
claims.fix: Replace controls[3].api.call and the rendered command with 'New-DlpPolicy -NewPolicy <policyDefinition>'. Move 'Module: Microsoft.PowerApps.Administration.PowerShell' to the row note rather than including it as an executable parenthesised expression.

claims.claim: Connector data policies can cover MCP connector consumption.
claims.quote:
To prevent agent makers from using Power Platform connectors as tools in Copilot Studio agents, configure a data policy with the connectors you want to block.
Blocking Power Platform connectors also blocks access to tools in connected MCP servers
claims.fix: Cite https://learn.microsoft.com/microsoft-copilot-studio/admin-data-loss-prevention and rename this row 'Connector data policies for MCP tools consumed by Copilot Studio agents'. Add the note 'This does not establish that classic data policies govern direct calls to the management MCP endpoint.'

claims.claim: Management-server-specific administrative UI and automation for DLP and server/tool access policy configuration are not documented.
claims.quote: Searched: '"MCPManagement" "DLP"'; '"management MCP" disable admin DLP access control audit permissions'; '"MCPManagement" admin UI disable Power Platform API pac admin settings'. Opened mcp-management and Agent 365 developer experiences; no such configuration is described.

claims.claim: Advanced connector policies can block an entire listed MCP server.
claims.quote: Within advanced connector policies, administrators can see MCP servers listed alongside other connector types and can choose to block an entire MCP server.

claims.claim: Advanced connector policies do not currently provide individual MCP tool control.
claims.quote: As of now, granular control over individual MCP tools (endpoints and actions) within an MCP server isn't available. Blocking the entire MCP server is supported.

claims.claim: Advanced connector policies are not confirmed to govern the direct management endpoint.
claims.quote: Searched: '"MCPManagement" "DLP"'; '"management MCP" disable admin DLP access control audit permissions'. Opened advanced-connector-policies and mcp-management; neither names direct management-endpoint coverage.

claims.claim: New MCP servers can expose connector data to any client allowed to call them.
claims.quote: Searched: '"management MCP server" "data" "client"'; '"MCPManagement" "access" "control"'. Opened management reference and Agent 365 developer experiences; neither defines this universal client/data-access relationship.
claims.fix: Replace the bullet with 'New MCP servers can include tools backed by connectors and APIs; confirm the data permissions and client access before adoption.' The tool composition is documented at https://learn.microsoft.com/microsoft-copilot-studio/mcp-management; the access relationship is not.

claims.claim: The prepare action rating fits an automatically enabled, high-risk change targeted for December 2026 on a 17 November 2026 run.
claims.quote: action: "prepare"; defaultState: "on"; risk: "high"; targetDate: "December CY2026". The standard defines act-now for automatic arrival targeted within about 60 days when risk or cost is medium or higher and a decision is needed.
claims.fix: Set action to 'act-now': the December month-only target is counted from 1 December, within 60 days of 17 November, and the briefing already identifies a pre-arrival decision about who may create and publish servers.

claims.claim: The governance table accounts for the tool-call monitoring that the checklist tells administrators to review.
claims.quote: After rollout: 'Review tool calls that change data.' Open questions: 'What auditing exists for server changes?' The controls table has no tool-call audit or monitoring control.
claims.fix: Remove 'Review tool calls that change data' from the checklist until a documented review surface is available; retain the open question rather than implying an operational monitoring control has been established.
